title: etcd Backup & Restore
summary: Snapshot etcd with etcdctl, check and restore it with etcdutl, and size the cluster for quorum.

items: etcd is the key-value store that holds **all** Kubernetes objects.
Regular backups let you recover from disasters such as losing every control plane node.
A snapshot contains all cluster state, including sensitive data, so **encrypt** snapshot files.
Access to etcd is equivalent to root on the cluster. Ideally only the API server talks to it.
Back up etcd before upgrading it, too.

rows: A running cluster, over the network
Keys and values, cluster admin, health, `snapshot save`
Restoring snapshots, checking snapshot status, defragmenting, migrating data

blocks.text: You may need both. `etcdctl snapshot status` and `etcdctl snapshot restore` are deprecated since etcd v3.5.x and slated for removal in v3.6; use `etcdutl` for those.
Use `etcdctl snapshot save` against a live member. Taking it doesn't affect the member's performance. Against a TLS-secured etcd you pass the endpoint and the client certificates:

items: Find the CA, cert and key file paths in the description of the etcd Pod.
The page's secure-client example uses `/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ca.crt`, `/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.crt` and `/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.key`.
Alternative: copy the `member/snap/db` file from an etcd data directory that no etcd process is using.
**Volume snapshot**: if etcd sits on a storage volume that supports backup (such as Amazon EBS), snapshot the volume instead.

blocks.text: Don't memorise the paths: take the trusted CA, cert and key from the etcd Pod's description, map them to `--cacert`, `--cert` and `--key`, and remember `ETCDCTL_API=3` and `--endpoints`.
The table shows the snapshot's **HASH**, **REVISION**, **TOTAL KEYS** and **TOTAL SIZE**. The older `etcdctl --write-out=table snapshot status` still prints the table but warns that it is deprecated.

Don't restore etcd while API servers are running. Stop every API server, restore all etcd instances, then start the API servers again. Also restart kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager and the kubelet so they don't rely on stale data.

items: `--data-dir` names a directory that the restore **creates**.
Reusing the old directory? Stop etcd and delete it before restoring.

Using a new directory? In `/etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml`, point the `etcd-data` volume's `hostPath.path` at it, then `kubectl -n kube-system delete pod <name-of-etcd-pod>` or `systemctl restart kubelet.service` (or both).
If the restored cluster's URLs changed, restart the API servers with the new `--etcd-servers` value (or update the load balancer in front of etcd).
Snapshots restore across patch versions of the same etcd major.minor.
Run etcd with an **odd number** of members. Recommended minimum versions in production: 3.4.29+ and 3.5.11+.
A **five-member** cluster is recommended for production. Don't autoscale etcd; going from three to five members is a reasonable way to gain reliability.
Scaling out improves availability at the cost of performance, not capacity.
If a **majority** of members fail permanently, the etcd cluster has failed: running Pods may keep going, but no new Pods can be scheduled and nothing in the cluster can change.
Replace failed members promptly and one by one: `etcdctl member remove <id>`, then `etcdctl member add <name> --peer-urls=<url>`.

options.text: In the description of the etcd Pod

questions.stem: True or false: Taking an etcd snapshot with `etcdctl snapshot save` slows the member down noticeably.

options.explanation: The page says creating it does not affect performance.
Correct. Snapshotting does not affect the member's performance.

options.text: Stop all API server instances first

options.text: Restore state in all etcd instances
options.explanation: Every instance is restored.

options.text: Restart all API servers, and also restart kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager and kubelet
options.explanation: Recommended so components don't use stale data.

options.text: Keep one API server running to serve reads during the restore
options.explanation: The page says to stop all API servers.

options.text: Running Pods may continue, but no new Pods can be scheduled and no state can change
options.explanation: The etcd cluster is considered failed.

options.text: Nothing; the API server caches all writes
options.explanation: Kubernetes cannot change its state.

options.text: All running Pods are killed immediately
options.explanation: Scheduled Pods might keep running.

questions.stem: One member of a three-member etcd cluster has failed. What does the page recommend?

options.text: Replace it promptly: etcdctl member remove <id>, then etcdctl member add with the new peer URL
options.explanation: Replacing a failed member is remove then add.

options.text: Restore every member from a snapshot
options.explanation: The cluster still has quorum; restore is for a failed cluster.

options.text: Leave it; etcd tolerates minor failures indefinitely
options.explanation: Replace failed members immediately for overall health.
